html:
The Late Antique Little Ice Age was a cold spell in the Northern Hemisphere that began about 536 CE and lasted roughly to 660. It was one of the coldest stretches of the last 2,000 years.

It began with the volcanic winter of 536, when volcanic dust dimmed the sun. Another eruption followed in 540 or 541. Tree rings show cold summers across Europe and Asia, and written sources report dim skies, failed harvests and hunger. Cold and hunger came just before the Plague of Justinian reached Constantinople in 541, and the two together fell on an empire already at war in Italy.

Historians still argue how much the cold changed events. Some link it to the weakening of the Eastern Roman Empire, migrations on the steppe and trouble in China and Persia. The causes are better known than the effects, and the effects were uneven from place to place.

The later Little Ice Age is a separate and much later cold period.
